text.en: Heat milk to just below the boil (scald it) rather than to a full boil.
text.de: Milch bis knapp unter den Siedepunkt erhitzen (abbrühen) und nicht voll aufkochen.

why.en: Just below the boil is hot enough. Fresh milk does not curdle from boiling alone; it curdles when it is old or meets acid.
why.de: Knapp unter dem Siedepunkt ist heiß genug. Frische Milch gerinnt nicht allein durch Kochen; sie gerinnt, wenn sie alt ist oder auf Säure trifft.

sources.title: Flavors of the Saucier: Stocks, Sauces and Soups (Zeringue and Thibodeaux)
sources.place: chapter 1.5 Bechamel Based Sauces, definition Scalded Milk
sources.sentence: to heat a liquid, usually milk, to just below boiling point. Boiling can cause the milk to curdle, which is not particularly appetizing.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004
sources.place: chapter Milk and Dairy Products, Milk Proteins (paragraph before 'The Caseins'), p. 19
sources.sentence: Fresh milk and cream can be boiled down to a fraction of their volume without curdling.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004
sources.place: chapter Eggs, Always Add Hot Ingredients to Cold, p. 94
sources.sentence: A custard mixed cold has just as even a texture and sets almost as quickly as a pre-scalded one.
